points.title: 童年与教育
points.description: 席勒1759年11月10日出生于符腾堡公国马尔巴赫的一个中产阶级家庭。他的父亲是军医，母亲是面包师的女儿。席勒从小就展现出对文学的热爱，但在父亲的坚持下，他于1773年被送往卡尔军事学院学习法律，这违背了他的个人意愿。在卡尔学院，席勒接触到了启蒙思想，并开始创作早期作品。这段时期的教育虽然严格，但为他后来的文学创作奠定了基础，同时也培养了他对自由的渴望和对专制制度的批判精神。
points.descriptionEn: Schiller was born on November 10, 1759, in Marbach am Neckar, in the Duchy of Württemberg, to a middle-class family. His father was an army surgeon, and his mother was the daughter of a baker. From an early age, Schiller showed a passion for literature, but against his wishes, his father enrolled him in the Karlsschule in 1773 to study law. At the military academy, Schiller was exposed to Enlightenment ideas and began his early literary works. This strict education, though contrary to his personal desires, laid the foundation for his later literary career and nurtured his longing for freedom and critical spirit towards authoritarian systems.

points.title: 军医与早期创作
points.description: 1780年，席勒从卡尔学院毕业，成为斯图加特的一名军医。尽管医学工作占据了他的大部分时间，席勒仍坚持文学创作。1781年，他创作了第一部戏剧《强盗》，这部作品在1782年首演后立即引起轰动，使他一举成名。然而，席勒因未经许可擅自离开军营观看首演而被监禁，随后被禁止发表任何作品。这一时期，他秘密创作了《阴谋与爱情》，并于1784年完成。1787年，席勒辞去军医职务，前往魏玛，开始专注于文学创作，摆脱了军事束缚，为他的文学事业开辟了新天地。
points.descriptionEn: In 1780, Schiller graduated from the Karlsschule and became a military surgeon in Stuttgart. Despite his medical duties consuming most of his time, Schiller continued to write literature. In 1781, he wrote his first play, 'The Robbers,' which caused a sensation upon its premiere in 1782, making him famous overnight. However, Schiller was imprisoned for leaving his post without permission to attend the premiere, and subsequently banned from publishing any works. During this period, he secretly wrote 'Intrigue and Love,' completed in 1784. In 1787, Schiller resigned his military post and moved to Weimar to focus on literary writing, breaking free from military constraints and opening new horizons for his literary career.

points.title: 历史学家与教授
points.description: 1789年，席勒接受耶拿大学的邀请，担任历史学教授。在耶拿期间，他不仅教授历史，还深入研究历史哲学，发表了《历史研究》等重要著作。同时，他继续创作戏剧，完成了《华伦斯坦》三部曲、《玛丽亚·斯图亚特》和《奥尔良的姑娘》等作品。1791年，席勒因健康问题陷入经济困境，但得到了丹麦赞助人的资助，使他得以继续创作。1792年，他因《强盗》被授予法国荣誉公民称号。在耶拿的十年间，席勒完成了从纯粹戏剧创作向历史哲学思考的转变，形成了自己独特的历史观和美学理论。
points.descriptionEn: In 1789, Schiller accepted an invitation to the University of Jena to become a professor of history. During his time in Jena, he not only taught history but also delved into historical philosophy, publishing important works like 'On the Study of Universal History.' Concurrently, he continued to write plays, completing the 'Wallenstein' trilogy, 'Mary Stuart,' and 'The Maid of Orleans.' In 1791, Schiller faced financial difficulties due to health issues but received support from Danish patrons, enabling him to continue his work. In 1792, he was awarded honorary French citizenship for 'The Robbers.' During his decade in Jena, Schiller evolved from purely dramatic writing to historical philosophical reflection, developing his unique historical perspective and aesthetic theories.

points.title: 成熟期与巅峰
points.description: 1799年，席勒应歌德的邀请移居魏玛，与这位德国文学大师开始了密切的合作。在魏玛的六年是席勒创作生涯的巅峰时期。他与歌德共同创办了《时序》杂志，推动了德国古典文学的繁荣。席勒完成了他最重要的戏剧作品，包括《威廉·退尔》、《墨西拿的新娘》和《华伦斯坦》的最终版本。他还创作了著名的《美学书信》，系统阐述了他的美学思想。1805年5月9日，席勒因肺结核在魏玛去世，年仅45岁。在魏玛的最后岁月里，席勒与歌德的友谊成为德国文学史上的一段佳话，他们的合作被称为'魏玛古典主义'，对德国文学产生了深远影响。
points.descriptionEn: In 1799, Schiller moved to Weimar at the invitation of Goethe, beginning a close collaboration with this German literary master. The six years in Weimar represented the peak of Schiller's creative career. With Goethe, he co-founded the journal 'Horen' and promoted the flourishing of German classical literature. Schiller completed his most important dramatic works, including 'William Tell,' 'The Bride of Messina,' and the final version of 'Wallenstein.' He also wrote his famous 'Letters on the Aesthetic Education of Man,' systematically阐述ing his aesthetic philosophy. On May 9, 1805, Schiller died of tuberculosis in Weimar at the age of 45. In his final years in Weimar, Schiller's friendship with Goethe became a legendary chapter in German literary history, and their collaboration came to be known as 'Weimar Classicism,' exerting a profound influence on German literature.

points.title: 逝世与遗产
points.description: 席勒于1805年5月9日在魏玛逝世，被安葬在雅各布公墓。他的早逝使德国文学界失去了一位伟大的天才。席勒的遗体后来于1827年与歌德一同移至魏玛历史公墓。席勒去世后，他的作品和思想继续影响着德国乃至世界文学。他的戏剧作品成为德国剧院的经典剧目，他的美学理论对后世艺术理论产生深远影响。1839年，德国作家和学者开始收集整理席勒的全集，为后世研究提供了宝贵资料。席勒的名字与歌德一起，成为德国古典文学的象征，他的自由精神和人文理想至今仍激励着无数读者和艺术家。
points.descriptionEn: Schiller died on May 9, 1805, in Weimar and was buried in the Jacobsfriedhof. His early death deprived the German literary world of a great genius. His remains were later moved to the Historical Cemetery in Weimar, alongside Goethe, in 1827. After his death, Schiller's works and ideas continued to influence German and world literature. His plays became classics in German theaters, and his aesthetic theories had a profound impact on later art theory. In 1839, German writers and scholars began collecting and editing Schiller's complete works, providing valuable resources for future research. Schiller's name, together with Goethe's, became a symbol of German classical literature, and his spirit of freedom and human ideals continue to inspire countless readers and artists to this day.

appraisal.zh: 席勒通常被视为德国古典文学的核心人物，与歌德并称德国文学的双子星，其剧作与美学思想深刻塑造了德国的民族认同与文化教育，作品至今在世界舞台上常演不衰。不过也有研究者指出，他笔下人物常是抽象理念的化身，理想化色彩浓厚，后期政治立场趋于保守，美学理论又偏重道德教化而轻艺术自律，其历史著作亦被指道德判断过重。
appraisal.en: Schiller is generally regarded as a central figure of German classicism, paired with Goethe as the twin stars of German literature; his plays and aesthetic thought shaped German national identity and cultural education, and his works are still widely performed worldwide. Yet some researchers note that his characters often embody abstract ideas, that his later political stance grew conservative, and that his aesthetics overemphasized moral education at the expense of artistic autonomy, while his historical writings have been faulted for excessive moral judgment.

supporter.zh: 席勒被德国浪漫主义者和自由主义者视为民族英雄和启蒙思想的代表。他的作品充满对自由的渴望和对专制的批判，激励了19世纪德国的民族统一运动。席勒与歌德的合作被誉为德国文学的黄金时代，他们共同创立的魏玛古典主义成为德国文化的骄傲。席勒的美学理论强调艺术的教育功能，认为美能使人达到道德自由，这一思想对德国教育体系产生了深远影响。他的戏剧作品至今仍在德国和世界舞台上广泛演出，证明了其艺术价值的永恒性。
supporter.en: Schiller is regarded by German romantics and liberals as a national hero and a representative of Enlightenment thought. His works, filled with longing for freedom and criticism of tyranny, inspired the German unification movement of the 19th century. Schiller's collaboration with Goethe is hailed as the golden age of German literature, and their Weimar Classicism became a source of German cultural pride. Schiller's aesthetic theory, emphasizing the educational function of art and the idea that beauty can lead to moral freedom, has profoundly influenced the German educational system. His plays continue to be widely performed in Germany and worldwide, demonstrating the timelessness of their artistic value.

critic.zh: 批评者认为席勒的作品过于理想化，缺乏对现实社会的深刻洞察。他的戏剧中的人物常常是抽象理念的化身，而非真实可信的个体。此外，席勒后期作品中的政治立场变得保守，对法国大革命的热情逐渐冷却，转向了对现有秩序的维护。一些评论家指出，席勒的美学理论过于强调道德教化，忽视了艺术的独立性和审美价值。他的历史著作也被批评为过于注重道德判断而缺乏客观性，反映了启蒙时代的历史局限性。
critic.en: Critics argue that Schiller's works are overly idealized and lack profound insight into real society. His characters often serve as embodiments of abstract ideas rather than believable individuals. Furthermore, Schiller's political stance became conservative in his later works, with his enthusiasm for the French Revolution cooling as he shifted toward maintaining the existing order. Some commentators point out that Schiller's aesthetic theory overemphasizes moral education at the expense of the independence and aesthetic value of art. His historical works have also been criticized for focusing too much on moral judgment rather than objectivity, reflecting the historical limitations of the Enlightenment era.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，席勒被定位为德国古典文学的核心人物之一，与歌德并称为德国文学的'双子星'。他的作品跨越了启蒙运动和浪漫主义两个时期，体现了德国文化的转型。席勒的戏剧不仅是文学经典，也成为德国民族认同的重要组成部分。他的美学思想影响了从康德到尼采的德国哲学传统。在当代，席勒的名字已成为德国文化教育的象征，他的肖像出现在德国10欧元纸币上，反映了他在德国文化中的崇高地位。席勒的作品被翻译成多种语言，在全球范围内持续产生影响，证明了其跨文化价值。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Schiller is positioned as one of the central figures of German classical literature, often mentioned alongside Goethe as the 'twin stars' of German literature. His works span both the Enlightenment and Romantic periods, reflecting the transformation of German culture. Schiller's plays are not only literary classics but also important components of German national identity. His aesthetic ideas influenced the German philosophical tradition from Kant to Nietzsche. In contemporary times, Schiller's name has become a symbol of German cultural education, and his portrait appears on the 10-euro banknote, reflecting his esteemed position in German culture. Schiller's works have been translated into multiple languages and continue to have a global impact, demonstrating their cross-cultural value.

self.zh: 人啊，只有当你是完全意义上的人，你才游戏；只有当你游戏时，你才是完全的人。
self.en: Man only plays when he is in the fullest sense of the word a man, and he is only completely a man when he plays.
